rules.why: Presenting a plan only keeps it waiting; the user approves it in the form.
Verify runs the unit's tests for an approved plan and keeps the receipt.
step_done makes its own checks (verify, files, secrets) before the harness commits.
The git block judges its command by the git rules itself and runs it only with the user's word where they ask.
A revision only waits for the user's approval again.
Dropping a waiting plan approves nothing; its revisions stay.
A skip gives up a step; its behaviours are kept skipped.
An annotation is a judgment marked as the model's; no gate reads it, and it changes no plan and no file.
The backfill only adds token usage read from the session transcripts and list prices to the ledger; it changes no plan and no file.
Settling ends only proven plans, or unproven plans of dead sessions after the user's Yes in a form.
git.commit judges its files by the plan, the verify and the commit guards itself.
git.push judges the push like git push in a shell, and refuses the home and protected branches.
A merge request opens only after the user confirms its full text in a form.
Lock commits only the acceptance tests the user approved with the delegated plan, on that plan's own branch, and pushes that branch; it refuses once a child has started.
tickets opens only one issue per child of the delegated plan the user approved, holding only its card, and writes its ticket file; it refuses once a child has started.
Recording a started child writes its crew entry only after the user approved the delegated plan in the form; the action refuses outside that grant and above the cap.
take opens only the card plan a brief named, approved by the grant of the parent plan the user approved in a form; it refuses a session that is no child.
A child pushes only its own branch, judged by the git rules like git push in a shell.
A child's question is only kept on its ticket; the model sends it to the orchestrator.
The handback commits only its receipt through the commit gate and pushes the child's own branch through the git rules.
A check only fetches a child's branch into a temporary checkout and runs its unit's tests; it writes the result on the crew entry.
Accept opens one pull request from a checked child's branch into its unit's base, as the user's delegated plan says; it merges nothing.
A send-back is recorded on the crew entry; the model sends it with send_message.
An answer is recorded on the crew entry; the model sends it with send_message.
Forgetting a child only records it; its session stays until the user agrees to archive it.
Land merges only the pull requests of children the parent accepted under the user's delegated plan, stops at a conflict, and closes the plan only on green tests.
Releasing a child only records that its session is the user's again; nothing is deleted.
Remove archives nothing itself: it marks only the children the user ticked in its checklist, one pass each, and names the archive calls.
An export only copies the ledger to a temp folder for the store; it changes no row and uploads nothing itself.
